correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the interval/complement bijection. The complement of one residue in each block has exactly 2tau entries; its jth pair produces precisely the stated T_j. The three cases partition r>2j, r=2j, r<2j and obey explicit invariant inequalities on S=[4,kappa]. Initial r0=a+6 is prolongable; the resulting A is strictly increasing, and substitution plus complement enumeration verifies A_n=a B_{2n-1}+3 B_{2n} for every n. The explicit deterministic base-tau automaton then follows. A direct exact-arithmetic verifier from an actual standalone file compared 75,000 greedy terms and 5,576,800 transitions; finite tests do not replace proof.

originality.rationale: Primary full-text comparison: Fokkink-Joshi Theorem 4 is A1-bounded and covers last coefficient <=2, with only the individual (1,3) outside that bound. The new infinite family (a,3), a>=2, is not an implication of these results; Bosma et al. concern all-one anti-bonacci cases. The exact uniform morphism and offset closure were separately derived, and targeted literature, mathematical-record, and prior-claim searches found no covering statement. Residual risk of an unindexed or different-formulation earlier theorem is explicitly retained.

value.rationale: The automaticity conjecture is open beyond the published A1-bounded restriction, and (a,3), a>=2, is the first natural infinite family immediately outside its order-two terminal-coefficient boundary. This settles infinitely many non-A1-bounded forms with arbitrarily large first coefficient by a new uniform invariant alphabet and explicit morphism, establishes exact block occupancy and an arithmetic subsequence, and bounds automaton states. The known (1,3) example is excluded from novelty; this is not arbitrary numeric slicing or mere restatement of the prior criterion.
